info.title: Acta API
info.description: Acta's operator API, the one the dashboard uses. Lists page by cursor: pass a page's nextCursor back as cursor until hasMore is false; a cursor is tied to its query. Every POST, PATCH, and DELETE is a control, mapped only where the host enables controls, and where the host requires it the call carries the confirmation header the operation lists, with the value true. POST /jobs answers 201 when it inserted the job and 200 when a deduplication key matched an existing one, with the job's URL in Location either way.

AcknowledgeAlertResponse.description: What acknowledging an alert did, and its timestamps after the attempt.

AlertDeliveryStatusCode.description:
Delivery state of one alert row. Numeric bands are a readability convention only; behavior
follows the explicit members.

AlertKindCode.description:
What condition an alert reports. Sparse catalog ids leave insertion room; numeric ordering is
not behavioral.

AlertRef.description:
Public stable reference for one alert row: "alr_" plus the Guid's 32 lowercase hex digits, such as
`alr_01a14f5038c17d0e9b2f6a4c81d3e5f7`. Dashboards, HTTP APIs, and alert transports address
alerts by this value; the numeric alert id stays the internal engine identity. Deduplication never
re-mints it: a condition that re-fires while its incident is open keeps that incident's ref.

CalendarRoleCode.description:
What a catalog calendar family gives a schedule: its occurrences, or the windows they may fire in. The family's first
version fixes its role, and every newer version keeps it.

CalendarStatusCode.description:
Where one version of a catalog calendar family stands. At most one version of a family is Published at a time, and
that version is the family's current one; a version's content never changes, only its status.

CalendarWindow.description:
One open range of an availability calendar: `[StartUtc, EndUtc)`, both UTC, the end after the start; a null
end is open forever.

CancelJobResponse.description: What cancelling a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

CheckpointKindCode.description:
Discriminator for `checkpoints` rows: which durable substrate feature owns the
`(job_id, checkpoint_kind_code, checkpoint_name)` slot. One physical table carries every simple job-internal
durable slot; the kind keeps the name spaces structurally separate (a user variable can never
collide with a signal or a child latch of the same name).

ControlAction.description: Coarse outcome of a control verb: on jobs, schedules, definitions, alerts, the outbox, tags, tenants, and namespaces.

DeadlineBehaviorCode.description: How the engine treats a job that has passed its deadline.

DefinitionPolicyOverrides.description:
The whole operator-override set for a definition's policy, applied as a unit: a non-null field sets its override
and null clears it back to the code default, so the dashboard reads, edits, and writes the full set. Code defaults,
contract, formats, and `definition_hash` are never touched. A `DeadlineSeconds` override on a scheduled
definition lands but is ignored: a deadline anchors to job creation, and a recurring slot lives forever.
`RateLimit` applies to every definition sharing the meter (declared `RateName`, or the name) in one
write, clearing included, so the meter never carries two rates.

DiscardOutboxResponse.description: What parking a discard of a source's quarantined rows did.

EnqueueJobAction.description: Coarse outcome classifier for one enqueued row.

EnqueueJobResponse.description:
What one enqueue answers: the internal long EnqueueJobResponse.JobId, the public JobRef EnqueueJobResponse.JobRef, and the
EnqueueJobAction EnqueueJobResponse.Action that tells a fresh insert from a match on string? EnqueueJobRequest.DeduplicationKey. A
batch answers one per request, in request order, in IReadOnlyList<EnqueueJobResponse> EnqueueJobsResponse.Jobs. A typed enqueue answers
the derived JobHandle.

EntityCode.description:
Names a kind of Acta entity, so one `(entity_code, entity_id)` pair can point at a row of any table. Tags
attach only to tenants, namespaces, definitions, and jobs, the targets TagTarget can build.

EvaluationStatusCode.description:
Why a schedule's next evaluation is when it is: the scheduling engine's state for one schedule, distinct from the
operator lifecycle (ScheduleStatusCode) and from the slot job's status.

EventCode.description:
Stable family-local event identifiers. Nearby values improve catalog readability but carry no runtime subject,
subgroup, or outcome semantics; match events by enum member or textual code. There is no `job.enqueued`
event on purpose: the Job row's own `(created_at_utc, namespace_id, definition_id)` records the enqueue fact,
and a separate event row would be write amplification on the narrow append-heavy events table; dedup outcomes
reach the caller via `EnqueueJobResponse.Action`, and cross-job rate analytics query `acta.jobs` directly.

FiringFailurePolicyCode.description:
What happens to a scheduled definition's schedules when a firing fails for good: its attempts are
spent, or an exception is not retryable.

GetAlertResponse.description:
The single-alert read model returned by ValueTask<GetAlertResponse?> IAlerts.GetAsync(AlertRef alertRef, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)). It carries the list row's fields today and
is a distinct type because a detail read can grow additively (delivery history, the alerting event's detail)
without the list row paying for it. Two delivery fields read differently than their names suggest:
`RetryCount` is the attempts spent in the current send series, not over the row's life (a delivered send
ends the series and resets it), and `RetryAfterUtc` is the earliest instant the alert may be sent again, the
next retry while delivery is unsettled or the next reminder once it has settled, null when nothing is scheduled.

GetCalendarDependent.description:
A schedule that names the family: its path, how it names the family (as its occurrence source or its availability
filter), its status (orphaned ones are listed), and its definition's delivery. A shared family's dependents span
namespaces, so the path carries the namespace. The name resolves at every evaluation, a calendar declared in the
process before the catalog's, so a dependent follows the family's current version unless its process declares one.

GetCalendarResponse.description:
One catalog calendar family as ValueTask<GetCalendarResponse?> ICalendars.GetAsync(CalendarLookup calendar, int? version = null, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) reads it. `CurrentVersion` is the Published
version, null while the family has none; `Versions` lists every version newest first; `Definition` is the
JSON of `ShownVersion`; `Dependents` lists every schedule that names the family in its scope, by job name and
then schedule name.

GetCalendarVersion.description:
One version of a family in IReadOnlyList<GetCalendarVersion> GetCalendarResponse.Versions: its status, the hash of its content, when it was
saved and last written, and when it was published, null for a version that never was.

GetDefinitionResponse.description:
The whole `definitions` row ValueTask<GetDefinitionResponse?> IDefinitions.GetAsync(string jobNamespace, string jobName, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) returns, in column order: identity and
control, contract and formats, each policy as its code default, operator override (null inherits), and
effective value, and audit bookkeeping. The dashboard's definition editor reads it; the grid reads the slimmer
ListDefinitionsItem. A definition is addressed by namespace and name, and its catalog id stays off
the wire.

inputFormatName.description: The name of JobPayloadFormat GetInputTemplateResponse.InputFormat, such as `json`, which is how the wire names a format.

GetInputTemplateResponse.description:
The input contract of a registered job as operator tooling sees it: the job it was asked for, the CLR input type
name, the wire format its input serializes to, and (Json inputs only) a compile-time JSON skeleton the enqueue form
can seed its editor with. Compile-time facts from the generated manifest; the template is a shape hint, never a
contract and never a default value.

GetJobExplanationAction.description:
A suggested operator move. string GetJobExplanationAction.Kind is a stable slug
(`raise-signal` | `cancel` | `resume` | `restart` | `inspect-timeline` |
`wait-recovery` | `none`); string GetJobExplanationAction.Description is the prose shown to the operator.

GetJobExplanationLease.description:
The execution lease on an Executing Job and the liveness of the worker holding it. When
bool GetJobExplanationLease.Expired is true the lease has lapsed and crash recovery reclaims the Job on its next pass;
string GetJobExplanationLease.RecoveryExpectation says so in prose. string? GetJobExplanationLease.WorkerName is the worker's deployment version, and
bool GetJobExplanationLease.WorkerStale is true once it has missed heartbeats past `JobsOptions.WorkerDeadAfter`. Both
WorkerRef? GetJobExplanationLease.WorkerRef and string? GetJobExplanationLease.WorkerName go null when retention purged the owner's row: the timings
still describe the Job, but the holder is unidentifiable.

GetJobExplanationResponse.description:
Plain-English explanation of a Job's current durable state: where the work is, why it moved there, and what an
operator can do next, assembled from the same `jobs_state`, `workers`, `steps`, `checkpoints`, and
`events` rows a `SELECT` would read. Returned by ValueTask<GetJobExplanationResponse?> IJobs.ExplainAsync(JobLookup job, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)); the CLI renders it as
prose, the dashboard as a panel. `Headline` is a one-sentence summary and `StatusMeaning` the
`[Code]` description of `Status`; `ActiveWait` and `Lease` are set only in the relevant states,
`LastExecutedBy` names the last worker when no lease is live, and `NextActions` are the operator's moves.

GetJobExplanationStep.description: One step slot's state, with string GetJobExplanationStep.Explanation rendering it as a plain-English clause.

GetJobExplanationWait.description: The durable wait a Suspended Job is blocked on: a signal name, or a timer slot and its due instant.

GetJobLineageMapChild.description: A direct child of the focused Job, linkable to its own detail view.

GetJobLineageMapNode.description:
A Job node in the lineage map - the focused Job or one of its ancestors. Carries the public
JobRef GetJobLineageMapNode.JobRef forms alongside the JSON-hidden numeric ids, matching ListJobsItem.

GetJobLineageMapResponse.description:
A compact runtime truth map for one focused Job: the ancestor context up to the lineage root, the focused Job with
its steps and the durable wait it is blocked on, and its direct children. Returned by
ValueTask<GetJobLineageMapResponse?> IJobs.GetLineageMapAsync(JobLookup job, GetJobLineageMapOptions? options = null, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)); the dashboard renders it as a lineage panel. V1 is shallow: `Ancestors`
is context only (root first, immediate parent last, no steps of their own), `Job` is the focused subtree root,
and `Children` are the direct children capped at int GetJobLineageMapOptions.ChildLimit with
`ChildrenHasMore` flagging a truncated set.

GetJobLineageMapStep.description: One step slot of the focused Job, with string GetJobLineageMapStep.Explanation its status in plain English.

GetJobLineageMapWait.description: The durable wait the focused Job is blocked on: a signal, child latch, or timer slot, and its due instant.

GetJobResponse.description:
Read projection of a Job row exposed by `IJobs.GetAsync`: identity, linkage, status, scheduling, leasing,
retention, and input format; the input payload itself is never returned. Property order mirrors the `jobs`
entity (identity, scope and routing, caller keys, input) and then its 1:1 `jobs_state` row, so the shape reads
in schema order; a column resolved to a public value follows the id it came from, and the created/modified pair
closes the record. JSON carries the public refs and hides the numeric ids. `DefinitionId` is the surrogate
for the namespace+name pair, non-null because the row's definition_id is NOT NULL.

GetOverviewResponse.description:
One-shot health counters for the dashboard overview, computed on the database clock: ready jobs (all Ready plus
Suspended jobs whose durable wait has expired) and the oldest one's claimable age, executing and failed jobs,
unresolved alerts and the Critical ones among them, dead workers and stale ones (Active or Draining, not seen
within the stale threshold), schedules due inside the due-soon window and the most overdue one's lag, and the
executor capacity across live workers, which `ExecutingCount` can exceed: a finished job stays Executing
until its batched completion write commits.

GetTagsItem.description: One normalized tag attached to a target.

GetTagsResponse.description:
The tags attached to one existing target, returned by ValueTask<GetTagsResponse?> ITags.GetAsync(TagTarget target, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)): an immutable snapshot ordered by
normalized name using ordinal comparison, and empty when the target carries no tags.

GetTenantResponse.description:
The single-tenant read model returned by ValueTask<GetTenantResponse?> ITenants.GetAsync(string tenantName, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)). It carries the same fields as
ListTenantsItem today and is a distinct type because a detail read can grow additively (usage counts,
per-tenant policy) without the list row paying for it. `TenantId` is the DB-assigned id
`jobs.tenant_id` references, internal and never serialized, since a tenant is addressed by its unique
`TenantName`; `Status` Active resolves at enqueue and Suspended rejects it; `Version` is the row
version a CAS control verb takes as expected.

GetWorkerResponse.description: Durable operator detail for one worker process registration.

JobPriorityCode.description:
Claim-priority value for `jobs_state.job_priority_code`. Discrete five-tier code-system enum
(`Bulk` / `Normal` / `High` / `Critical` / `Realtime`); no intermediate
values. Strict priority ordering on claim (no aging, no anti-starvation budget), so operators
isolate bulk workloads in their own `JobNamespace`. Set by the definition policy, definition
override, or per-enqueue priority override.

JobRef.description:
Public stable reference for one Job row: "job_" plus the Guid's 32 lowercase hex digits, such as
`job_01a14f4e954e7bf68ac609f3fcad8e3d`. Dashboards, HTTP APIs, and clients address jobs by this
value; the numeric JobId stays the internal engine identity. It copies and searches as one word,
and a UUIDv7 reads in creation order.

ListAlertsItem.description:
One alert row in a ValueTask<ListAlertsResponse> IAlerts.ListAsync(ListAlertsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) page. Channel configuration, endpoints, and deduplication keys
are delivery internals, never exposed by list reads. JSON carries the public job ref and hides the numeric job id;
the ref goes null once the subject job row is purged, since alerts outlive their job. `RetryCount` is the
attempts spent in the current send series (a delivered send ends it), and `RetryAfterUtc` the earliest instant
the alert may be sent again, the next retry while delivery is unsettled or the next reminder once settled.

items.description: The page's alerts, at most `PageSize` of them.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the final page.

hasMore.description: Whether more alerts exist beyond this page.

pageSize.description: The effective page size after defaulting and clamping.

totalCount.description: The filter-wide count, populated only when the query set `IncludeTotal`.

ListAlertsResponse.description: One page of ValueTask<ListAlertsResponse> IAlerts.ListAsync(ListAlertsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)).

ListCalendarsItem.description:
One calendar family in a ValueTask<ListCalendarsResponse> ICalendars.ListAsync(ListCalendarsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) page. `CurrentVersion` and `PublishedAtUtc` are the
Published version's, null while the family has none; `LatestVersion`, `LatestStatus`, and `ModifiedAtUtc`
are the highest version's; `DependentCount` counts the schedules, orphans aside, that bind the family through the
catalog: the namespace's, or every namespace's for a shared family in `sys`.

items.description: The page's calendar families, at most `PageSize` of them.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the final page.

totalCount.description: The filter-wide count, populated only when the query set `IncludeTotal`.

ListCalendarsResponse.description: One page of ValueTask<ListCalendarsResponse> ICalendars.ListAsync(ListCalendarsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)).

ListDefinitionsItem.description:
One definition in an ValueTask<ListDefinitionsResponse> IDefinitions.ListAsync(ListDefinitionsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) page, trimmed to the dashboard grid: identity, status,
contract type names, the four policies the grid shows (priority, max attempts, concurrency limit, rate limit) as
override and effective so it can flag an operator override, and the rate name, which names the meter and so says
which definitions share it. GetDefinitionResponse carries the whole row. A definition is addressed by
namespace and name, and its catalog id stays off the wire.

ListEventsItem.description:
One event in a ValueTask<ListEventsResponse> ILedger.ListEventsAsync(ListEventsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) page. The subject is `EntityKind` and `EntityId`,
the one numeric id on the wire, because the subject outlives its row: a purged job's events, and its
`job.purged` tombstone, still name it. The joined refs and names (`JobRef` of a job subject,
`LineageRootJobRef`, `WorkerRef`, `TenantName`, `JobName`) are null when absent or once their
row is gone. `Message` is the human text; `DetailsText` is the details payload decoded to text, null when
the event carries none or a non-json format.

One job row in a ValueTask<ListJobsResponse> ILedger.ListJobsAsync(ListJobsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) page: identity, lifecycle, and audit-facing fields only; the
input payload is never exposed by list reads. JSON carries the public refs and hides the numeric ids.
`CorrelationKey` is the caller-supplied trace, request, or order id, `ExecutionNumber` the attempt
counter, and `FailureCount` the consecutive-failure count behind the retry budget.

One Quarantined staging row as the operator listing reports it: identity and routing fields (a null
correlation or tenant name was never set), when the producer staged it, and the failure evidence
(`FailureCount` delivery attempts consumed before quarantine, and the bounded `LastError`).
`OutboxId` is the producer-minted id a scoped requeue or discard targets. The payload never leaves
the producer's database.

One relay source as ValueTask<ListOutboxSourcesResponse> IOutbox.ListSourcesAsync(ListOutboxSourcesQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) reports it: the namespace's `sys.outbox` slot
(`SlotJobRef`, whose audit trail holds the operator evidence) plus the accounting of its last successful tick,
read from the slot's `outbox-status` variable: `LastTickSummary`, `Backlog` (pending rows still awaiting relay), and
`QuarantineTotal`, all null until the slot's first successful tick. `IsLocal` says this process
registered the source, so ValueTask<ListOutboxQuarantinedResponse> IOutbox.ListQuarantinedAsync(ListOutboxQuarantinedQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) works here.

ListSchedulesItem.description:
One schedule row in a ValueTask<ListSchedulesResponse> ISchedules.ListAsync(ListSchedulesQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) page. `NextOccurrenceAtUtc` is the next undecided occurrence;
`NextEvaluationAtUtc` and `EvaluationStatus` say when and why the engine next looks; `Status` is Active, Paused,
or Orphaned, with `PausedUntilUtc` for a timed pause; `Version` is the row version a CAS control verb takes as
expected; `JobRef` is the permanent slot's public ref, null for a PerOccurrence definition; `OutstandingCount` counts
its unsettled roots; the expiry pair is null together when unused, and `AvailabilityCalendarName` when the schedule
observes no availability calendar. The ids stay off the wire: the list pages by `ScheduleId` in its cursor.

NamespaceStatusCode.description:
Namespace state machine. 10-spaced ids; live states 10..80, mirroring
TenantStatusCode.

PauseJobResponse.description: What pausing a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

PauseScheduleResponse.description: What pausing a schedule did, and the schedule's state after the attempt.

PreviewCalendarItem.description: A schedule that names the family, as a publication would meet it: its path, binding, status, and overdue flag.

PreviewCalendarResponse.description:
A version's forecast beside the current version's over the same horizon, so an operator sees what a publication
adds and removes: instants for an occurrence calendar, windows for an availability calendar, and the bound
schedules with their overdue flag, which a Refuse publication would reject on.

PreviewScheduleResponse.description:
A read-only forecast of a schedule's upcoming fire instants, computed live (no persisted state is
read or written). string PreviewScheduleResponse.Expression and string PreviewScheduleResponse.TimeZoneId are the effective values
(operator override when present, else the original); IReadOnlyList<DateTime> PreviewScheduleResponse.NextOccurrencesUtc is strictly
increasing and may be shorter than requested when the expression is exhausted.

overdueDecision.description:
What a calendar publication does with the occurrences a dependent schedule has not decided yet that are already due
under the version it replaces.

PublishCalendarResponse.description:
The outcome of a publication: Applied with the version now current and the schedules retimed (as
`job/schedule` paths), NotFound when the candidate is no version of the family, VersionConflict when the
current version is not the one the caller saw, or Rejected with the reason and, when the old version left overdue
occurrences undecided, the schedules holding them.

PurgeJobResponse.description: What purging a job did, and the job's status after the attempt; a purge carries no version.

RaiseSignalResponse.description: What raising a signal on a job did, and the job's status after the attempt; a raise carries no version.

RegisterTenantResponse.description:
The tenant a registration created or found: its stable numeric id, and its canonical key, which is how every other
call and route addresses it.

RemoveTagsResponse.description: What removing one tag did: applied, or the target did not exist.

ReprioritizeJobResponse.description: What reprioritizing a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

RequeueOutboxResponse.description: What parking a requeue of a source's quarantined rows did.

RescheduleJobResponse.description: What rescheduling a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

ResolveAlertResponse.description: What resolving an alert did, and its timestamps after the attempt.

RestartJobResponse.description: What restarting a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

ResumeJobResponse.description: What resuming a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

ResumeNamespaceResponse.description: What resuming a namespace did, and the namespace's version after the attempt.

ResumeScheduleResponse.description: What resuming a schedule did, and the schedule's state after the attempt.

ResumeTenantResponse.description: What resuming a tenant did, and the tenant's version after the attempt.

RetireDefinitionResponse.description: What retiring a definition did, and the definition's version after the attempt.

SaveCalendarDraftResponse.description:
What saving a draft did. Applied carries the new version and its content hash; Rejected carries each reason in
`Problems`, a compiler problem starting with its JSON path, and, when the store refused it, the family's latest
version, 0 for a family with none. A namespace no worker has run in yet is created, so the save never answers NotFound.

ScheduledDeliveryCode.description:
How a schedule delivers a definition's work: one durable slot job fired again and again, or a fresh root job per
admitted occurrence. Immutable once the definition is registered.

ScheduleFullBehaviorCode.description: What a due occurrence does when its schedule already has its maximum of unsettled occurrences.

SetDefinitionOverridesResponse.description: What setting a definition's policy overrides did, and the definition's version after the attempt.

StepStatusCode.description:
State machine for `steps` rows. INSERT-once on first invocation (`Pending`);
UPDATE-in-place across retries; terminal transition to `Succeeded` (with `Result` populated),
`Exhausted` (parent receives `StepExhaustedException`), or `Interrupted` (an
`AtMostOnce` step re-entered before completion; parent receives `StepInterruptedException`). One row per
`(JobId, StepName)`; the framework never INSERTs a second step row for the same slot.

SuspendNamespaceResponse.description: What suspending a namespace did, and the namespace's version after the attempt.

SuspendTenantResponse.description: What suspending a tenant did, and the tenant's version after the attempt.

TagInput.description:
Caller-supplied per-tag wire row attached to an enqueued Job. Names are unique within a
request; string? TagInput.Value is null for presence-only tags.

TenantStatusCode.description: Tenant state machine. 10-spaced ids; live states 10..80.

TriggerScheduleNowResponse.description: What firing a schedule now did, and the schedule's state after the attempt.

UpdateJobInputResponse.description: What amending a job's input did, and the job's status after the attempt; an amend carries no version.

UpdateNamespaceResponse.description: What updating a namespace did, and the namespace's version after the attempt.

UpdateTenantResponse.description: What updating a tenant did, and the tenant's version after the attempt.

UpsertTagsResponse.description: What upserting one tag did: applied, or the target did not exist.

WorkerStatusCode.description:
Lifecycle status of a worker row. Mirrors the JobStatusCode band scheme: live states 10..90,
terminal success at 100, terminal error at 200+.
